title: CLCON/355/2019 of J. P. GANGWAR Vs VINAY KUMAR CHAUHAN

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
ON THE 23RD DAY OF MARCH, 2021
BEFORE:
HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI
CONTEMPT PETITION No. 355 of 2019
BETWEEN:
Dr. J.P. Gangwar. ..........Petitioner
(By Mr. Krishan Kumar Verma, Advocate)
AND:
Vinay Kumar Chauhan and another. ...Respondents
(By Mr. Ravi Babulkar and Mr. Davesh Bishnoi, Advocate
for respondent no. 1)
JUDGMENT
Learned counsel for respondent no. 1
submits that the order passed by Division Bench of
this Court has been complied with, inasmuch as,
petitioner has been re-instated in service and arrears
of salary has also been paid to him, except the period
for which he was employed elsewhere.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits
that petitioner was not gainfully employed elsewhere,
therefore, he is entitled to salary for the entire period,
during which he remained out of employment. He has
drawn attention to paragraph no. 7 of the objection
filed by petitioner in reply to the supplementary
affidavit filed by respondent no. 1, which is
reproduced below:

2
"7. That the contents of para 6 of the
supplementary reply are not admitted
as stated hence vehemently denied. It
is stated that the petitioner was never
appointed in the said college and there
is no approval of the Vice Chancellor of
the University for alleged appointment.
It is stated that petitioner has some
times engaged in the said college as
Guest Lecturer and only when he used
to give lecture he was paid some
remuneration in lieu of lecture and
there was not prescribed/fixed salary
of the petitioner regarding the said
working as guest lecturer. It is further
stated that the Hon'ble Writ Court has
not held in the order allowing writ
petition that if the petitioner was
employed elsewhere after his illegal
termination he would not entitled for
salary rather a clear cut direction has
been issued by the Hon'ble Writ Court
that petitioner be reinstated forthwith
and also directed to pay the arrears of
salary of petitioner from the date of
illegal termination. Hence the
reasoning given by respondent that as
petitioner was in alleged employment
therefore he was entitled for arrears
only till 26.1.2020 is absolutely
misconceived and is apparently
contempt of the order of this Hon'ble
Court."
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits
that although petitioner was engaged as a Guest
Teacher in some other college, but, he was never
appointed by the Competent Authority and his
appointment was never approved by the Competent
Authority i.e. Vice Chancellor of the concerned
University. He further submits that petitioner did not
receive any salary for the period, during which he
rendered services as Guest Teacher, but he was paid
some remuneration for the number of lecturers, he
gave.

3
4. Learned counsel for the respondent no. 1
has handed over a cheque amounting to ` 5,11,226/-
to learned counsel for the petitioner, which has been
duly accepted by him on behalf of his client.
5. Since the order passed by Division Bench of
this Court has been substantially complied with,
therefore, nothing survives in this Contempt Petition.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits
that petitioner is entitled for some more amount
towards salary of 45 days, during which he served in
R.L.S. Memorial Degree College, Jaspur, District
Udham Singh Nagar. If that is so, petitioner shall be
at liberty to approach appropriate forum for claiming
the said salary.
7. In such view of the matter, the Contempt
Petition is closed.
8. Contempt notices issued to the respondents
are hereby discharged.
 (MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI, J.)
Arpan
